extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Area Chairs at CVPR 2026 on managing reviewer selection, moderating discussions, running triplet meetings, writing meta-reviews, and making accept/reject/placement recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will suggest reviewers for each paper that is assigned to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend first browsing the paper, think about related work that is cited and closely related work you are aware of. Suggest a diverse group of reviewers from multiple institutions and geographic regions. Do not only suggest the top-ranked reviewers listed by OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag desk-rejectable submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag papers for desk rejection, e.g., if papers exceed the length restrictions even by a single character, or if an incorrect template was used to write the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During reviewer-suggestion period ACs will also flag such papers. Be strict about obvious policy/template/length violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure each paper has at least three quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your aim is to get at least 3 quality reviews for each paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are due on Jan 12 and will be released to authors on Jan 22. Prior to Jan 20, ensure reviewers have completed reviews, send reminders, find and assign emergency reviewers if needed. Emergency reviewers should be assigned no later than Jan 14. Contact emergency reviewer candidates via a personal email prior to assigning them if common practice. Escalate to senior AC if difficulties arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and remedy missing or delinquent reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviews are missing or reviewers are unresponsive, immediately start looking for and recruiting emergency/additional reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two main cases: assigned reviewers unresponsive after deadline, or additional reviews could improve confidence. Assign emergency reviewers using AC console after confirming availability. If you struggle, contact Senior AC or Program Chairs. Keep in mind responsibility to ensure all papers have three informed reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response period actions
rubrics_metrics.description: During author response period (Jan 22 - Jan 29), if any reviews are still missing, it is urgent to track them down or invite additional reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise no action should be needed from ACs during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate and oversee reviewer-author discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as the author response is entered, ACs should lead a discussion via OpenReview and make sure the reviewers engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize critical concerns when initiating discussion, ask reviewers whether they share the concern, encourage reviewers to comment specifically on which concerns were addressed by the rebuttal, and pinpoint critical issues to inform the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage active and focused reviewer engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the reviewers interact with the AC and among themselves, especially for papers with both positive and negative reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For borderline papers, ACs should go through all such papers and engage reviewers in discussion; ask targeted/individual questions (example: R2 mentioned unclear novelty — could R2 point to the most relevant works that overlap?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag problematic reviewer behavior or LLM usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag extremely delayed reviews, low-quality reviews, or papers with significant LLM usage not disclosed in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalate egregious violations of policies (author or reviewer) to the Senior AC or SAC as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and schedule AC triplet meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: As a LeadAC, initiate scheduling of triplet meetings to discuss borderline papers (meetings should happen Feb 6 - Feb 16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a spreadsheet summarizing each paper's contributions, reviewer assessments, and your recommendation. Present borderline papers, claimed contributions, reported results, and discuss key strengths/weaknesses. Aim to find consensus and involve Senior AC if consensus not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle borderline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Borderline papers are primarily identified by the spread of review scores and require focused discussion in triplets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the paper carefully prior to the triplet meeting and highlight key points. During meetings, discuss reviewer-identified strengths/weaknesses and aim for a consensus recommendation; if consensus cannot be reached, escalate to Senior AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a high-quality meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a high-quality meta-review that summarizes the paper’s contribution, highlights the main points of the reviewers’ initial assessment, discusses the rebuttal, summarizes reviewers’ reasons for their final recommendation, and concludes with the AC recommendation and underlying rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to write a meta-review of at least 60 words. The meta-review should be standalone, a clear decision rationale, and enable authors to understand why the decision was made. Avoid one-line delegations (e.g., 'all reviewers said reject' is not acceptable if a rebuttal was provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review structure: concise description of content
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise description of the submission’s main content (scientific claims and findings) based on your own reading and reviewers’ characterization, including the paper’s strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally include both what is discussed and what is missing from the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review structure: concise summary of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary of the discussion, listing points raised by reviewers, how each was addressed by authors in the rebuttal, whether reviewers have remaining concerns, and whether the AC found each point worth consideration in decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review structure: recommendation and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Your recommendation and justification: end with a clear indication of your recommendation and justify it based on the content and discussion of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider acceptance criteria (Award/Oral/Poster/Reject) when making and justifying placement recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance/placement criteria (Award/Oral/Poster/Reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested acceptance criteria to consider when recommending award, oral, poster, or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award: major advances that will heavily impact the field; will be used by many people, create new capabilities, etc. Oral: potential to be very significant; worthwhile for the whole community to hear about. Poster: incremental steps that expand community knowledge or add bricks to the cathedral of knowledge; papers introducing useful tools; papers of interest to a subcommunity. Reject: unlikely to be significant or already known — provide clear evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend papers for the findings track
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond accept-reject, ACs are asked to recommend papers for the findings track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend technically sound papers with solid experimental validation and contributing valuable insights, even if their technical novelty is more incremental (e.g., technically sound but incremental novelty). These may be discussed in triplet meetings and may not have received accept recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary AC approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary ACs need to approve the decision and meta-review of the primary AC by the meta-review deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review special category decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs respond to PC and SAC requests to recommend spotlight papers, oral papers, and award candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review special category decisions during Feb 21 - Feb 26 as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role: Reviewing Process Manager responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Help Program Chairs manage the reviewing process: recommend appropriate reviewers and assign alternate reviewers in a timely manner so every submission gets a fair evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select good reviewers at the beginning to help later; when reviewers are delinquent, assign alternates timely to ensure three quality reviews per paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role: Decision Maker responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: For every submission, recommend whether it should be accepted or rejected, accompanied by a meta-review summarizing the reviews and the discussion of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use triplet meetings for disagreements, flag papers for desk reject, participate/lead triplet meeting, write meta-reviews, ensure reviewers' judgments align with reviewer guidelines, and ensure language in reviews and meta-reviews is constructive and polite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role: Discussion Moderator responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderate each submission's discussion, encouraging and steering active, relevant discussion and discouraging irrelevant or toxic participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinpoint critical issues and ask how rebuttal addresses them; moderate so discussions focus on scientific merits, limitations, and clarifications; encourage reviewers to consider author rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role: Discussion Participant expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively participate in discussions as a scientific expert whose assessment is critical to the decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate not just as moderator but also contribute technical judgments and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle confidential comments appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs may receive confidential comments from authors and reviewers during review, rebuttal, and discussion processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to these comments and acknowledge receipt if appropriate so authors or reviewers know they are being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge each paper on its own merits (do NOT normalize within batch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT normalize decisions within your own batch; judge each paper on its own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A batch of papers is too small to reflect overall acceptance rates (example statistics provided). Base recommendations on individual merits rather than attempting to fit a local acceptance quota.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow unanimous reviewer consensus except rare exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow reviewer consensus for unanimous decisions unless there are extraordinary unusual circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: to accept with unanimously negative reviews requires significant referee error or a very convincing rebuttal; to reject with unanimously positive reviews requires exceptional circumstances such as significant undetected technical errors, fraud, or plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check reviews as they are submitted and catch fundamental errors early
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be checking reviews as they are submitted, and catching fundamental errors at that time, not during the triplet discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively monitor incoming reviews to identify issues early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze mixed reviews critically
rubrics_metrics.description: For mixed reviews, analyze all reviews critically and see if you agree with their claims; get help within your triplet when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use triplet discussion and consult SACs if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep discussions within triplets unless conflict-free outside opinion is needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your discussions within triplets; if you need a conflict-free outside opinion, reach out to your SAC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spilling deliberations broadly; escalate appropriately for conflict-free input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a standalone, explanatory meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: The meta-review should be a decision rationale that contains an argument why the paper should be accepted or rejected and provide sufficient and clear arguments so authors can understand the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid meta-reviews that merely defer to reviewers (e.g., 'all reviewers said reject, so the paper is rejected') especially if a rebuttal was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use review scores curves for individual decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: PCs do not plan to share the rating curve; ACs should not rely on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base your recommendations on the reviews as well as the contributions and merits of papers; SACs can help calibrate if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations about citation of recent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are authors expected to cite and discuss very recent work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers published within the last four months are considered contemporaneous. Authors are encouraged to cite all relevant papers; they may be excused for not knowing about papers not published in peer-reviewed proceedings or journals (e.g., arXiv).
